method: Each satellite is a unit line-of-sight row in the local east, north and up frame: east = -cos(el) sin(az), north = -cos(el) cos(az), up = -sin(el), with a fourth column of 1 for the receiver clock offset. Azimuth is degrees clockwise from true north and elevation is degrees above the horizon, so the geometry needs no site position, Earth model or orbital data. Satellites with an elevation below the mask (inclusive on the mask itself) are discarded before the normal matrix is formed; fewer than four usable satellites cannot give a 3D fix and is reported as an error. The normal matrix is the sum of the outer products of the used rows, a symmetric 4x4 matrix that is inverted by Gauss-Jordan elimination with partial pivoting; a pivot smaller than 1e-10, or any non-finite entry in the inverse, means the directions are geometrically dependent and no unique solution exists. With Q the inverse, GDOP is the square root of the trace of Q, PDOP of Q's position block, HDOP of its east and north terms, VDOP of the height term and TDOP of the clock term, so GDOP squared equals PDOP squared plus TDOP squared and PDOP squared equals HDOP squared plus VDOP squared. Values are rounded to four decimals and compared with the usual PDOP bands: 2 or less ideal, 5 or less excellent, 10 or less good, 20 or less moderate, above 20 poor. The accuracy estimate multiplies HDOP and VDOP by an assumed average range error, which treats range errors as independent and equal on every satellite; real receivers weight satellites by elevation and signal strength, and ionosphere, troposphere, multipath and orbit errors are not modelled, so the figures are a planning estimate rather than a guarantee. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Kaplan and Hegarty, Understanding GPS: Principles and Applications: the geometry matrix, dilution of precision and the relation between DOP and position error.
Standard DOP identities: GDOP^2 = PDOP^2 + TDOP^2 and PDOP^2 = HDOP^2 + VDOP^2, which follow from the trace of the inverse normal matrix.
GNSS receiver practice of screening a solution with an elevation mask and a DOP limit, for example rejecting fixes above a chosen HDOP or PDOP.
Golub and Van Loan, Matrix Computations: Gauss-Jordan elimination with partial pivoting for a small symmetric normal matrix.
